a.summary: The commit refreshed the tx baseline's `# line` metadata but left the README prose that supplies those rows' required written reasons pointing at pre-v1 line numbers, and several of its bullets document accepted mutants that no longer exist in tx-accepted.csv.
a.failure_scenario: A maintainer triaging `software.sava.core.tx.TransactionRecord,...` acceptances opens the tx section of the README as AGENTS.md directs (accepted rows need a written reason there) and reads at line 344 "`TransactionRecord.sign` 154: the multi-signer scan resolves a single signer to the same slot the fast path uses" as a currently-accepted equivalent. There is no `TransactionRecord,sign` row in tx-accepted.csv at all, and TransactionRecord.java:154/156 are blank and `tableAccountMetas()` — not `sign`. The reader concludes the suite carries accepted debt it does not carry, and cannot map any live CSV row to its justification because every line number in the section predates the v1 merge.

b.summary: The three pending-prune rows keep `# line 28` / `# line 37` / `# line 40` tags that point into the `DataEncoding` enum and `DATA_ENCODING_PARSER` lambda `0112d69` added, and the new section never says the tags are historical — the half of F3 that is still open.
b.failure_scenario: A reviewer follows `sava-core/config/pitest/README.md:63-64` ("The authoritative anchor is each row's `# line` tag in the CSV") to `responses-accepted.csv:2-4`, opens `JsonUtil.java` at lines 28, 37 and 40, and lands on `base58, base64, base64_zstd`, `return DataEncoding.base58;` and the lambda's closing `}` — code added *after* the rows were written, and belonging to `lambda$static$0`, not to `parseEncodedData` at all. The tags therefore read as a fresh re-anchoring onto new code rather than as pre-`0d68f02` history, which is exactly the misreading F3 reported. No sanctioned writer can fix this (`BaselineRetag` refreshes only matched rows, `sava-build/HARDENING.md:861-864`), so the README note is the only available remedy and it was not written.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
